title: Hybrid Search and Reranking
summary: Keyword and embedding retrievers fail on different queries, so production systems fuse them and then rerank a wide candidate list with a more accurate model. This lesson defines the retrieval metrics, works through Reciprocal Rank Fusion and shows how to size the retrieve-then-rerank funnel.
objectives: Compute recall@k, precision@k, MRR and nDCG for a ranked list by hand
Fuse two ranked lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k = 60) and compare it with weighted score fusion
Explain why a cross-encoder reranker raises precision and compute its latency from N, tokens and model size
Size N (candidates) and k (kept) from a recall target, a latency budget and a cost budget
Use maximal marginal relevance to reduce redundant context
prerequisites: You should know how BM25 and dense retrieval score documents, and the difference between a bi-encoder and a cross-encoder ([Term-Based and Embedding Retrieval](/learn/retrieval-and-rag/sparse-and-dense)). Index recall from [Vector Indexes](/learn/retrieval-and-rag/vector-indexes) is a different quantity from the retrieval metrics defined here.
